facts: A central problem of word sense disambiguation is the lack of manually sense-tagged data required for supervised learning.
WSD is an abbreviation for word sense disambiguation.
The paper evaluates an approach to automatically acquire sense-tagged training data.
The approach acquires sense-tagged training data from English-Chinese parallel corpora.
The English-Chinese parallel corpora are used for disambiguating the nouns in the SENSEVAL-2 English lexical sample task.
The method of acquiring sense-tagged data is promising.
On a subset of the most difficult SENSEVAL-2 nouns, the accuracy difference between the two approaches is 14.0%.
The accuracy difference could narrow further to 6.5% if the advantage that manually sense-tagged data have in their sense coverage is disregarded.
Manually sense-tagged data have an advantage in their sense coverage.
Supervised learning requires manually sense-tagged data.
Nouns in the SENSEVAL-2 English lexical sample task are disambiguated.
The issue of domain dependence is important in evaluating WSD programs.
The analysis highlights the importance of the issue of domain dependence in evaluating WSD programs.
The SENSEVAL-2 English lexical sample task contains nouns.
